Appearance:
 Shri Sanjay Gupta - advocate for the petitioner.
 Ms. Dr. Anjali Gyanani - P.P. - appearing on behalf of   ORDER
The applicant has filed this Second application u/S 483, BNSS for grant of bail.
First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 11/07/2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 24667/2024.

The applicant has been arrested by Police Station Crime Branch, District Gwalior in connection with crime No. 25/2024 registered for the offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 384,
120-B of IPC and section 66-D of I.T. Act.

entities.text: Police Station Crime Branch, District Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated.
He further argued that applicant is the only earning member of his family.
He further argued that applicant is business man and is reputed citizen of India.

It is further argued that the applicant is working in Xstream Industries, FZCO, Dubai as Director and General Manager of the said Company, against which, the applicant has also obtained license from Dubai Government.
It is further argued that the applicant is involved in the business of buying and selling crypto currency through himself as well as through his agents.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15661 2 MCRC-37194-2024
He further argued that there is no evidence to connect the applicant accused with the crime.
Main allegations are against co-accused Mir Mudassar and Kapil.
The applicant is in custody since 31/03/2024.

Learned counsel for the applicant has also placed reliance on the judgment delivered by the Apex Court vide judgment dated 09/08/2024 arising out of SLP (Cri) No. 8772/2024 (Manish Sisodia vs.
Directorate of Enforcement ).

sentences.text: The applicant is permanent resident of District Bhilai (Chattisgarh).
Conclusion of trial is likely to take time and there is no likelihood of his absconsion, if released on bail.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.

On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the application on the ground that applicant and other co-accused persons conspired and played fraud with the complainant, who lost Rs. 46 Lakh and 05 Lakhs total amounting to Rs. 51 Lakhs of her hard earned money.
It is further argued that there are sufficient evidence to show that the applicant has actively involved in conspiracy.
It is further argued that first application of the applicant was dismissed after detailed arguments vide order dated 11/07/2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 24667/2024.

Thereafter,
circumstances have not been changed and, therefore, there is no reason to allow this second bail application.

It is further submitted that bail application of co-accused Vikash and Manishankar have already been dismissed by this Court vide order dated 22/07/2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.
30602/2024 & 30603/2024.
It is further submitted that in this case serious allegations are made against the applicant - accused about his active participation in commission of the offence with co-accused Mir Mudassar.
The co-accused Mir Mudassar has transferred money into the account operated by the applicant - accused.

It is further submitted that on 13/04/2024 co-accused Mir Mudassar was arrested and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15661 3 MCRC-37194-2024 on the basis of investigation, it has been established that he frequently transferred money into the account of the present applicant.
There are sufficient evidence that the applicant contacted co-accused Mir Mudassar on the date of transferring money.
It is further argued that on the basis of memorandum of the applicant incriminating articles have also been recovered.

Under these circumstances and in view of gravity of offence prayed for rejection of the bail application by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record,
no case for grant of bail is made out.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.
On considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case particularly the nature of allegation as well as gravity of offence and the role played by the applicant, I am of the opinion that this is not a fit case, in which bail may be granted to the present applicant.
Accordingly, this Second application of the present applicant under Section 483 of BNSS relating to the aforesaid crime is hereby dismissed.
Certified copy as per rules.
